prompt: Write 10 distinct lessons the claims-triage agent (home and motor claims assessment within delegated authority) at Larkmere Mutual learned across many cases about: asking to pay a premium monthly instead. Each is a working pattern or tip for the next case, not about any one member, one or two sentences, in the agent's voice ("When…, …"). Return {"items": [{"type": "fact" | "preference" | "observation", "content": "..."}]} with exactly 10 items. (batch 1)
response: {"items":[{"type":"observation","content":"When a member says they cannot afford a full annual payment after a claim, asking whether they want to move to monthly payments can keep cover in place without delay and reduce the chance of cancellation."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a policy is due for renewal or reinstatement, I should confirm that monthly payment may add interest or fees before I offer it as a practical alternative to paying in one go."},{"type":"preference","content":"When the member sounds uncertain, I prefer to explain monthly payment as a budgeting option rather than a concession, so it feels normal and straightforward."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the loss is stressful, a simple question about monthly payment at the end of the call often lands better than introducing it early, because it does not distract from the claim itself."},{"type":"fact","content":"When a policy has already lapsed or is close to cancellation, I need to signpost that monthly payment may not be available straight away and may depend on a fresh underwriting decision."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a member has multiple household costs rising at once, offering monthly payment alongside the claim update can improve take-up because it addresses the wider affordability problem they are already describing."},{"type":"preference","content":"When I suggest monthly payment, I prefer to mention the direct debit date and the ongoing commitment clearly, so the member can judge whether it genuinely fits their budget."},{"type":"fact","content":"When there is an excess to pay as part of the claim, I should not imply that switching to monthly payments removes that immediate amount; the two are separate obligations."},{"type":"observation","content":"When a member asks for the cheapest way to keep cover, monthly payment is worth discussing, but it should be checked against any total cost difference over the year."},{"type":"observation","content":"When the case is otherwise straightforward and within delegated authority, raising monthly payment as an optional next step can resolve follow-up queries in the same contact and reduce repeat calls."}]}
